## Course Information

**MATH 346 Mathematical and Statistical Software**

**3 Lecture hours, 0 Laboratory hours, 3 Credits**

**Prerequisite:**

- COSC 114
- MATH 204 or MATH 211
- MATH 242 or MATH 243 or MATH 244

## Course Catalog Description

This course introduces mathematical and statistical programming using the MATLAB and R programming languages. The topics covered span a variety of topics in data science and numerical computation, including tidy data, exploratory data analysis, plotting, and symbolic computation.

## Textbook

A. Gilat, *MATLAB: An Introduction with Applications*, 6th Edition, Wiley, 2020, ISBN: 9781119299257.

## Reference Materials

H. Wickham and G. Grolemund, *R for Data Science: Import, Tidy, Transform, Visualize, and Model Data*, 2nd Edition, O'Reilly Media, 2023.

## Course Topics

| Week # | Topics |
|---|---|
| 01 | Arrays and script files in MATLAB |
| 02 | MATLAB: Programming, user functions |
| 03 | MATLAB: Curve fitting and interpolation |
| 04 | MATLAB: Built-in numerical analysis, 3d plotting |
| 05 | MATLAB: Symbolic Math |
| 06 | R: Markdown, and data visualization |
| 07 | R: Workflow, and Data Transformation |
| 08 | R: Exploratory Data Analysis |
| 09 | R: Tibbles, Data import, and Tidy data |
| 10 | R: Relational data, Strings, Factors, dates and times |
| 11 | R: Pipes and Functions |
| 12 | R: Vectors and iteration |
| 13 | R: Model basics and model building |
| 14 | R: Handling many models |
| 15 | R: Additional topics in visualization and communication |

## Structure and Learning Methodologies

Lectures will be 2 x 75-minutes per week. Students are required to practice the use of computer software on their laptops. Quizzes, assignments and projects are held throughout the semester to reinforce knowledge of the material.

## Computer Resources

Students are required to have individual access to MATLAB and R.

### Course Framing

The course follows the approved MATLAB and R syllabus. The teaching approach emphasizes reproducible, AI-aware computational work:

- formulate a mathematical or statistical problem;
- implement a solution in MATLAB or R;
- validate numerical, graphical, and statistical output;
- communicate the result in a reproducible report;
- document any generative AI assistance.

### Weekly Workload

For the common examination on 10 October, see the [midterm student
guide](../assessments/midterm.qmd). It covers Weeks 1-6 only; Week 7 is excluded.

The website is a complete resource bank; not every visible activity is due. In
an ordinary week, students attend the two class meetings, complete the
instructor-selected checkpoints of one guided main lab, attempt 4-6 core
exercises, and complete a short in-class exit check. AI-review labs are
embedded or assigned selectively rather than added automatically as a second
weekly submission.

Routine website-based practice outside class targets approximately 90-120
minutes in an ordinary week, excluding separately announced project work and
quiz or examination preparation. See the
[weekly workload guide](../weeks/workload-guide.qmd) for the exercise selection
and the meaning of core, guided, and extension work. Assessment weeks receive
a reduced selection when an assessment displaces normal class time.

### Software and Access

Students need reliable access to MATLAB for Weeks 1-5 and Project 1, and to R
for Weeks 6-15 and Project 2. Symbolic Math Toolbox is required for Week 5. The
R block uses `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `readr`, `tidyr`, `stringr`, and `lubridate`.
Quarto is required only to edit and render a supplied Week 6 scaffold; students
do not author either project report in Quarto.

Reliable access may be provided by a verified laboratory, an institutionally
licensed online route, or a personal installation. Students are not required
to purchase software or a paid generative-AI account. Git and GitHub are
optional and are not submission tools. See the
[software and access requirements](../resources/software-requirements.qmd) for
the complete matrix and runnable setup checks.

### Project Structure

Each project team may contain one, two, or three students. Three students is the
maximum. Groups of two are allowed, and a student may choose to work alone as a
one-person team. The same project requirements, deadlines, and grading criteria
apply to every team size. Team members may be enrolled in either class session.
A cross-session team receives one group identifier, one assigned dataset, and
one group grade; each student continues to attend their registered class
session.

**Project 1:** MATLAB numerical investigation using a group-specific synthetic
building-energy dataset. The complete group package is due through Blackboard
on Thursday, 24 September 2026, at 23:55 UAE time.

**Project 2:** R data analysis, modeling, and validation using richer training
data and a withheld validation file, due around Week 15.

The project stages are fixed relative to the teaching sequence:

| Project | Preview | Group package | Checkpoint and later release | Completion window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Project 1 | Week 3 | MATLAB package in Week 4 | Readiness check in the first Week 5 session | Thursday, 24 September 2026, 23:55 UAE time |
| Project 2 | Weeks 9-10 | R training package in Week 12 | Frozen plan after Week 13; validation in Week 14 | Week 15; exact date announced later |

The [project milestone map](../projects/project-milestones.qmd) explains what is
released through Blackboard and what students do at each gate. Confirmed dates
are published on the relevant assessment or project page; Blackboard remains
authoritative for access windows and submission logistics.

Students submit a PDF report together with executable source code and required
machine-readable results. They are not required to find or collect a dataset,
write Quarto, or write HTML. All synthetic data must be identified as synthetic,
and every project includes a responsible AI-use appendix and group-contribution
statement.

Projects are group-assessed. Individual competence is established through the
quizzes, semester examination, and final examination. Any group member may be
invited to a brief project verification, selected randomly or because submitted
work requires clarification. Selection does not imply suspected misconduct, and
a project–examination grade difference is not evidence by itself.

### Missed Assessments And Late Project Submissions

#### Quizzes

- There are no make-up quizzes.
- A student who misses a scheduled quiz without an absence approved by the
  Registrar's Office receives a grade of zero for that quiz.
- If the Registrar's Office confirms that the absence is approved, the quiz
  grade is replaced by:
  - the semester-examination (midterm) grade when the quiz took place before
    the semester examination;
  - the final-examination grade when the quiz took place after the semester
    examination.

### Semester Examination (Midterm)

- There is no make-up semester examination.
- A student who misses the scheduled semester examination without an absence
  approved by the Registrar's Office receives a grade of zero for it.
- If the Registrar's Office confirms that the absence is approved, the final-
  examination grade is also assigned as the semester-examination grade.

A maximum of **40% of the course grade** can be compensated through the
approved-absence substitutions above.

#### Projects

Late project submissions are penalized at **10% per day or part of a day**.
The number of late days is rounded up.

### Classroom Policies

Discipline and punctuality are important components of academic and
professional success. Students should make every effort to arrive before the
class begins at the time shown in Banner. Late arrival distracts both the
instructor and other students.

A student who arrives **more than five minutes after the scheduled beginning
of class will be recorded as absent for that class**. The student should
nevertheless enter quietly, avoid interrupting the class, and participate in
the remainder of the session.

If a student is absent from, or late to, a class, the student is responsible
for reviewing the missed material, checking Blackboard for announcements, and
obtaining any instructions provided during the class. The instructor is not
responsible for repeating an entire missed class individually.

A student arriving after an in-class quiz has begun may take it only while it
remains available. The common closing time is not extended because of late
arrival, except for an approved accommodation or an officially approved
exceptional circumstance.

Exceptional circumstances are handled in accordance with applicable university
procedures.
